 Crystal Crop Protection IPO GMP at ₹19; subscription 1.46x
 Reviewed by Multibagg AI Research Desk Nov 18, 2026, 09:31 PM IST • 2 min read Add as preferred source on Google Key highlights
 Crystal Crop Protection IPO was subscribed 1.46 times in the latest reported Day 1 update.
 The latest reported GMP was ₹19 per share, implying an indicative price of ₹291 against the ₹272 upper band.
 The ₹455.49-crore issue has a ₹259-272 price band and a retail lot size of 55 shares.
 Crystal Crop Protection IPO closes on November 20, with tentative listing scheduled for November 26.
 powered by IRIS 
 Crystal Crop Protection IPO showed a grey market premium of ₹19 per share and total subscription of 1.46 times on November 18, 2026, based on the latest figures in the available updates. At the ₹272 upper price band, the ₹19 GMP indicates an estimated ₹291 listing price, though GMP is unofficial and can change.
 What is the Crystal Crop Protection IPO subscription status?
 Crystal Crop Protection IPO was subscribed 1.46 times in the reported Day 1 update, pointing to moderate demand across the issue. The public offer opened on November 18 and will close on November 20, giving investors a three-day subscription window.
 The category-wise data showed qualified institutional buyers subscribing 2.11 times, retail individual investors 1.35 times and non-institutional investors 0.79 times. The employee portion was subscribed 3.11 times. Within the non-institutional segment, the sHNI category was subscribed 1.09 times, while bHNI subscription stood at 0.64 times.
 Earlier updates from the same day showed different stages of demand. At 10:20 am, the issue had received 6% subscription, with bids for 7,86,280 shares against 1,21,70,076 shares on offer. Another Day 1 update said the IPO was fully subscribed, with bids for 1,22,16,105 shares against 1,21,70,076 shares offered, illustrating how subscription figures changed as bids came in.
 What does the Crystal Crop Protection IPO GMP indicate?
 Crystal Crop Protection IPO's latest reported grey market premium was ₹19 per share as of 6:30 pm IST on November 18. Added to the upper price band of ₹272, this produces an indicative price of ₹291 and an implied premium of about 7%.
 Other available reports placed the GMP at ₹13, or around 5%, which implied an estimated listing price of ₹285. A separate update cited a GMP of ₹18 and an estimated listing price of about ₹290. These differing figures reflect the unofficial nature of grey market quotations and their movement through the day.
 GMP is not part of the regulated IPO process and does not assure a listing gain. The eventual market price will depend on demand and market conditions when Crystal Crop Protection shares are proposed to begin trading on November 26.
 Got a follow-up? Ask IRIS
 How does Crystal Crop Protection's ₹455.49-crore issue split between fresh shares and the offer for sale? What does the ₹136-crore anchor investment indicate about pre-IPO institutional participation? How could changes in the GMP before November 26 affect expectations for the listing day? What are the Crystal Crop Protection IPO price and dates?
 Crystal Crop Protection IPO has a price band of ₹259 to ₹272 per share, with investors required to bid for at least 55 shares. At the upper end of the band, one retail lot requires ₹14,960, excluding applicable charges.
 The ₹455.49-crore issue consists of a fresh issue of 1.31 crore equity shares worth ₹354.77 crore and an offer for sale of 37.03 lakh shares worth ₹100.71 crore. The net offer allocation reserves 50% for qualified institutional buyers, 35% for retail investors and 15% for non-institutional investors.
 The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on November 23. Refunds and credit of shares to successful applicants' demat accounts are scheduled for November 25, followed by the tentative BSE and NSE listing on November 26. Eligible employees applying in the employee reservation portion receive a ₹25-per-share discount.
 Conclusion
 Crystal Crop Protection IPO entered its subscription period with total demand of 1.46 times in the latest available Day 1 data and a reported GMP of ₹19. Institutional demand at 2.11 times was higher than retail demand at 1.35 times and non-institutional demand at 0.79 times, while the grey market suggested only a modest premium over the issue price.
 Investors will watch subscription trends through the November 20 close, particularly changes in QIB, retail and NII participation. The next disclosed milestones are the expected allotment finalisation on November 23, demat credit and refunds on November 25, and the tentative listing on November 26.
